name: ramp_get_attention_feed
description:
Return the authenticated user's homepage attention feed.

Use this tool to see what needs the user's attention right now: pending approvals,
missing receipts, overdue reviews, signatures, and similar action items that appear
on the Ramp homepage.

By default, the tool returns the default homepage sections with compact
LIST-hydrated task rows. To fetch more from a section, pass that section's
section_type and next_cursor back in sections.

For own-card GET_ATTENTION_FEED remediation, use this as the canonical task feed.
blocking_effects describes a task type's possible sanction, not proof that an item
caused the active lock. Use browser_handoff for user action in Ramp. For an
available CompleteTransactionRevision, inspect or edit the transaction and call
it with a nonblank reason. Re-read both tools and continue relevant overdue tasks;
success requires the task absent, blocking_task_count=0, and is_spendable=true.
Pending verification is not an unlock.

name: ramp_get_funds
description:
Retrieve funds (cards or budgets) and their balances, restrictions, locks, owners,
or permitted spend. For a named person's funds, resolve their UUID with GetOrgChart
and pass user_uuids. For the current user's funds, use MY_FUNDS. Search by fund name
with search_by_fund_display_name or look up a known UUID with fund_uuid.

Every fund includes balance_data. Treat its remaining amount as authoritative for cleared
charges, pending authorizations, and applicable rollover. limit_amount excludes rollover;
accrued_rollover_amount is the opening carry, already included in remaining_amount.
Do not add rollover or subtract spending again. Never infer that
a booking is included merely because it is confirmed: a postpaid booking with no charge or
pending authorization is a future charge and has not yet reduced the remaining balance.

A fund with a lock can't be spent from until it is unlocked, even though it is ACTIVE
and keeps its remaining amount. Never present a locked fund as available; mention it
separately with its lock reason, without quoting its remaining amount as money left
unless the user asks what it holds once unlocked. A member lock blocks only that member.

Set True to return only funds that are active AND have virtual cards enabled — the only funds an agent card can be minted on. Set False to return the funds that cannot. Leave unset to return funds regardless of agent-card eligibility. Every returned fund also carries an `agent_card_eligible` flag.

name: ramp_reporting_query
description:
Use for aggregate questions (totals, trends, top-N, comparisons, breakdowns) over Ramp data and for canonical financial statements from authorized connected ERP books. Data is eventually consistent (may lag a few minutes).

Execute a semantic reporting query and return typed rows.

Before querying, find and load the relevant reporting skill and follow its guidance.
Requires a dataset and its query contract from the semantic catalog.
Financial-statement datasets accept `statement.time_window`, optional
provider-dimension `statement.filters`, and a response-size `limit`. They
return fixed, canonically ordered account and calculated-total rows with
provider currency and publication metadata. These overlapping rows must
not be summed. SQL controls, comparisons, and top-N scope are unsupported;
missing or changed ledger publications return a failed-precondition error.

For SQL datasets, `report_query` is a ReportQuery: dataset, dimensions, measures,
filters, post-aggregation having or aggregate-filter clauses, optional time
range, per-dimension ranking, ordering, and limit. A `filters` clause whose
`field` is a catalog field is a row predicate; one whose `field` is a
selected measure output name (its `name` alias when present) is the
preferred aggregate predicate and applies after grouping (HAVING), e.g.
`{"field": "txn_count", "op": "gt", "value": 3}`. `having` and
`aggregate_filters` remain supported equivalents, but are deprecated and
migrated into `filters`; `result_metadata.predicate_migration` records the
migration.
Order by any selected orderable dimension or measure output.

For complete SQL results, set `page_size` (1–1,000) to paginate. Pass
`response.table.page.next` as `start` with the same `report_query`,
`query_scope`, and `page_size` until it is null. Pages read live data, not
a snapshot. Financial statements and `second_stage` / `post_aggregation`
queries do not support pagination.

A measure ref may carry its own `filters` plus a unique `name` to emit a
conditional aggregate column ("sumIf"). Select the same measure several
times with different filters for side-by-side cohort columns, e.g. one
spend total per category grouped by user, including an "other" column via
a NOT_IN filter. Measure filters use the same field/op/value shape as
query filters but only base-dataset fields.
A catalog entry with non-empty `aggregations` also accepts a ref with
`agg` (`type` from `aggregations`) and a required `name`. If `covered_by`
lists a measure for that agg, select that measure instead.
Use `second_stage` whenever the question aggregates per-group results
again (days/months/vendors per X, average monthly spend per X, highest or
lowest month per X, users over $X per month): retain `dimensions` and
compute `measures`, each `{"agg": SUM|AVG|MIN|MAX|COUNT, "of":
<first-stage measure output name or null>, "name"}`, across the collapsed
groups, instead of post-processing first-stage rows yourself. COUNT
without `of` counts groups that survive the aggregate predicates (a
measure-output `filters` clause or the deprecated forms, which migrate
like any other query); only a stage made solely of such counts needs a
predicate, so never add a threshold just to satisfy it when
SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX or COUNT of an operand is present. For example, select
user plus `{"field": "spend_date", "time_grain": "day"}`, filter
daily_spend over $500, then use `{"dimensions": ["user"], "measures":
[{"agg": "COUNT", "name": "days_over_limit"}]}`; retain `spend_date`
instead to count users over the threshold per day or month. For average
monthly spend per vendor, select vendor and month with `{"measure":
"amount", "name": "monthly_spend"}` and use `{"agg": "AVG", "of":
"monthly_spend", "name": "avg_monthly_spend"}`: an average of monthly
totals over the months that have spend (a month with no rows is not a
zero), so present it as an average per active month or add a COUNT of
months; MIN/MAX of the same operand give each vendor's lowest and highest
month. Operands must be selected first-stage measure outputs (aliases
allowed), never window measures. Order by retained dimensions or stage
names only; `limit` applies to the final rows; no `totals`. Use user with
amount for employee spend; only per-diem or meal questions need attendee
with amount_per_attendee, which allocates across Ramp employee attendees
only (external attendees are excluded) and falls back to the spending
employee when no attendee list exists. Keep the daily grain so day counts
are by UTC calendar day. `post_aggregation` (`{"dimension", "name"}`) is
the deprecated equivalent of a single COUNT stage; do not use it for new
queries.

Use `max_groups` for K named values plus Other independently on every
selected non-time dimension, retaining all time buckets. Set
`ranking_order_by` to selected first-stage measure scores. When the time
range is omitted, ranking covers all authorized data. Display `order_by`
is separate. Omit `limit`; without `page_size`, ranked results have a
1,000-row cap disclosed through result_metadata.is_truncated. Ranking
cannot combine with aggregate predicates or second_stage.

query_scope.title: query_scope
query_scope.description: Result-set scope. Use complete for all, each, every, or otherwise unrestricted results. Omit report_query.limit; complete overrides any supplied flat limit and uses 1000 rows per response unless page_size enables pagination. Use complete with max_groups; it preserves per-dimension ranking. Use top_n only when the user explicitly requested exactly N rows, and set report_query.limit to that N. Financial statements do not support top_n; complete preserves their canonical order. Omission preserves the query limit.

- `DRAFT_PARSING`: The draft bill is being parsed (e.g., via OCR).
- `DRAFT_MISSING_INFO`: The draft bill is missing required information.

- `DRAFT_QUEUED`: The draft bill is queued for automatic conversion to a bill upon vendor approval.
- `APPROVAL_PENDING`: The bill is waiting for one or more approvals.
- `AWAITING_RELEASE`: The bill is waiting for payment release.
- `PAYMENT_READY`: The bill is ready for payment.
- `PAYMENT_ERROR`: The bill payment failed.
- `ON_HOLD`: The bill has been placed on hold.
- `BLOCKED`: The bill is blocked from payment initiation or approval.
- `HELD_BY_PROVIDER`: The bill payment is held by the payment provider.
- `PENDING_VENDOR_APPROVAL`: The bill is waiting for a vendor edit to be approved.
- `PAYMENT_DETAILS_MISSING`: The bill is missing required payment details.
- `PAYMENT_NOT_INSTRUCTED`: The bill uses Ramp payments but has not been scheduled yet.
- `WAITING_FOR_TRANSACTION_MATCH`: The bill is paid by card and is waiting for a matching card transaction.
- `WAITING_FOR_TRANSFER_MATCH`: The bill is paid by direct debit and is waiting for a matching wallet transfer.
- `WAITING_FOR_VENDOR`: The bill is waiting on required vendor information.
- `AWAITING_PAYMENT`: The bill is waiting for the business to send push-payment funding.
- `PAYMENT_PROCESSING`: The bill payment has been initiated and is processing.
- `PAYMENT_SCHEDULED`: The bill payment is scheduled.
- `PAYMENT_COMPLETED`: The bill has been paid.
- `ARCHIVED`: The bill has been archived.

chosen ``selected_outbound_offer_id`` and the same modifications to retrieve
matching returns. Split-ticket bookings change one leg per exchange: when
several legs are passed, only the earliest requested leg is searched and
``deferred_leg_indexes`` lists the others to change afterwards in their own
searches. ``selected_outbound_offer_id`` is rejected for split-ticket bookings.

Some bookings support the first search but not this second step, and return an
unsupported-provider result with support details; route the traveler to that
support rather than retrying. Search prices are estimates; call
SubmitFlightModification to re-quote the selected offer with the airline before
asking the traveler to confirm.

``recommended_offers`` is always present, ranked from this page of ``offers``;
each surface presents those entries in the format it supports, and
``assistant_note`` states which presentation applies.

Preference fields (``cabin_class``, ``max_stops``, ``airlines``, timing
windows, ``avoid_red_eye_flights``) become this booking's cumulative
modification preference state: they carry across the outbound and return
steps and later re-searches of the same booking. Omitted preferences retain
their prior values; use ``clear_preferences`` only when the traveler removes

description:
Search for flights and return policy-tagged offers ready to quote. Before first use in a conversation, load and follow the ramp-book-flight skill when available.

Tell the tool what to search (route + dates), or give it a job_id - never both. Start a NEW interactive search with wait_for_results=false: it returns a job_id immediately, so ask the traveler's unresolved preferences while the search runs and resume with the same job_id on a later call. Blocking (wait_for_results=true, the default when omitted) is the exception for flows that need a complete result immediately and cannot resume later.

A call with job_id reads cached results and never starts another provider search. Use job_id alone with wait_for_results=true to read the completed first page, add cursor to read the next page, add preferences to change the filtered or ranked view, or add sort_key to change its order; omit cursor when making either change so the new view starts at its first page.

For a round trip, start the search with return_date. The first response contains OUTBOUND offers with is_round_trip=true and round-trip totals. Choose an outbound offer, then call with its job_id and outbound_offer_id to get matching RETURN offers. The chosen return offer's id identifies the complete outbound-and-return itinerary for booking. To filter return offers (e.g. by airline), pass the same job_id and outbound_offer_id with the new preference - do not start a new search, which discards the selected outbound flight and reruns the entire provider query.

A completed outbound response includes web_search_url for the cached search in Ramp Travel. Fare options are nested under their flight, and a nested fare option id can be selected for return offers. Search preferences are cabin_class, required_upgrade_cabin_class, airlines, max_stops, only_split_tickets, preferred_departure_time_window, preferred_arrival_time_window, and avoid_red_eye_flights; omitted preferences retain their prior values, and applied_preferences reports what each response used.

Omit cabin_class unless the traveler names a cabin; omitted, recommendations use the highest in-policy cabin unless a saved cabin preference applies.

Do NOT use this tool to change, modify, or cancel an existing booking in place. It may search for a separate replacement flight only when a loaded skill, such as ramp-rebook-flight, directs it.
